pairs: Post hæc abiit Jesus trans mare Galilææ,
After these things, Jesus traveled across the sea of Galilee,
which is the Sea of Tiberias.
And a great multitude was following him,
quia videbant signa quæ faciebat super his qui infirmabantur.
for they saw the signs that he was accomplishing toward those who were infirm.
Subiit ergo in montem Jesus et ibi sedebat cum discipulis suis.
Therefore, Jesus went onto a mountain, and he sat down there with his disciples.
Erat autem proximum Pascha dies festus Judæorum.
Now the Passover, the feast day of the Jews, was near.
et vidisset quia multitudo maxima venit ad eum,
when Jesus had lifted up his eyes and had seen that a very great multitude came to him,
But he said this to test him.
ipse enim sciebat quid esset facturus.
For he himself knew what he would do.
Ducentorum denariorum panes non sufficiunt eis, ut unusquisque modicum quid accipiat.
“Two hundred denarii of bread would not be sufficient for each of them to receive even a little.”
Dicit ei unus ex discipulis ejus,
the brother of Simon Peter, said to him:
Est puer unus hic qui habet quinque panes hordeaceos
who has five barley loaves and two fish.
sed hæc quid sunt inter tantos?
But what are these among so many?”
“Have the men sit down to eat.”
Erat autem fœnum multum in loco.
Now, there was much grass in that place.
in number about five thousand, sat down to eat.
and when he had given thanks,
he distributed it to those who were sitting down to eat;
similiter et ex piscibus quantum volebant.
similarly also, from the fish, as much as they wanted.
Colligite quæ superaverunt fragmenta, ne pereant.
“Gather the fragments that are left over, lest they be lost.”
et impleverunt duodecim cophinos fragmentorum ex quinque panibus hordeaceis,
and they filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves,
which were left over from those who had eaten.
Illi ergo homines cum vidissent quod Jesus fecerat signum,
Therefore, those men, when they had seen that Jesus had accomplished a sign,
Quia hic est vere propheta, qui venturus est in mundum.
“Truly, this one is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
Jesus ergo cum cognovisset quia venturi essent ut raperent eum, et facerent eum regem,
And so, when he realized that they were going to come and take him away and make him king,
fugit iterum in montem ipse solus.
Jesus fled back to the mountain, by himself alone.
his disciples descended to the sea.
And when they had climbed into a boat,
they went across the sea to Capernaum.
et non venerat ad eos Jesus.
and Jesus had not returned to them.
Mare autem, vento magno flante, exsurgebat.
Then the sea was stirred up by a great wind that was blowing.
Cum remigassent ergo quasi stadia viginti quinque
when they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia,
they saw Jesus walking on the sea,
and drawing near to the boat,
Voluerunt ergo accipere eum in navim
et statim navis fuit ad terram,
they were willing to receive him into the boat.
But immediately the boat was at the land to which they were going.
turba, quæ stabat trans mare, vidit quia navicula alia non erat ibi nisi una,
the crowd which was standing across the sea saw that there were no other small boats in that place,
et quia non introisset cum discipulis suis Jesus in navim,
except one, and that Jesus had not entered into the boat with his disciples,
but that his disciples had departed alone.
aliæ vero supervenerunt naves a Tiberiade juxta locum ubi manducaverant panem, gratias agente Domino.
Yet truly, other boats came over from Tiberias, next to the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks.
Cum ergo vidisset turba quia Jesus non esset ibi,
Therefore, when the crowd had seen that Jesus was not there,
neque discipuli ejus, ascenderunt in naviculas,
nor his disciples, they climbed into the small boats,
and they went to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
Et cum invenissent eum trans mare,
And when they had found him across the sea,
quæritis me non quia vidistis signa,
not because you have seen signs,
but because you have eaten from the bread and were satisfied.
Do not work for food that perishes,
sed qui permanet in vitam æternam,
but for that which endures to eternal life,
which the Son of man will give to you.
For God the Father has sealed him.”
Quid faciemus ut operemur opera Dei?
“What should we do, so that we may labor in the works of God?”
ut credatis in eum quem misit ille.
that you believe in him whom he sent.”
And so they said to him:
Quod ergo tu facis signum ut videamus
so that we may see it and believe in you?
Patres nostri manducaverunt manna in deserto,
Our fathers ate manna in the desert,
just as it has been written,
Panem de cælo dedit eis manducare.
‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
non Moyses dedit vobis panem de cælo,
Moses did not give you bread from heaven,
sed Pater meus dat vobis panem de cælo verum.
but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
Panis enim Dei est, qui de cælo descendit, et dat vitam mundo.
For the bread of God is he who descends from heaven and gives life to the world.”
And so they said to him,
qui venit ad me, non esuriet,
Whoever comes to me shall not hunger,
et qui credit in me, non sitiet umquam.
and whoever believes in me shall never thirst.
that even though you have seen me,
Omne quod dat mihi Pater, ad me veniet:
All that the Father gives to me shall come to me.
et eum qui venit ad me,
not to do my own will,
sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me.
but the will of him who sent me.
Hæc est autem voluntas ejus qui misit me,
Yet this is the will of the Father who sent me:
Patris: ut omne quod dedit mihi, non perdam ex eo,
that I should lose nothing out of all that he has given to me,
sed resuscitem illud in novissimo die.
but that I should raise them up on the last day.
Hæc est autem voluntas Patris mei,
this is the will of my Father who sent me:
ut omnis qui videt Filium et credit in eum,
that everyone who sees the Son
and believes in him may have eternal life,
et ego resuscitabo eum in novissimo die.
and I will raise him up on the last day.”
Therefore, the Jews murmured about him,
Nonne hic est Jesus filius Joseph,
whose father and mother we know?
“Do not choose to murmur among yourselves.
No one is able to come to me,
et ego resuscitabo eum in novissimo die.
And I will raise him up on the last day.
It has been written in the Prophets:
‘And they shall all be taught by God.’
Omnis qui audivit a Patre, et didicit, venit ad me.
Everyone who has listened and learned from the Father comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father,
nisi is, qui est a Deo,
except he who is from God;
this one has seen the Father.
whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Patres vestri manducaverunt manna in deserto,
Your fathers ate manna in the desert,
Hic est panis de cælo descendens:
This is the bread which descends from heaven,
ut si quis ex ipso manducaverit,
so that if anyone will eat from it,
Si quis manducaverit ex hoc pane,
If anyone eats from this bread,
And the bread that I will give is my flesh,
caro mea est pro mundi vita.
for the life of the world.”
Litigabant ergo Judæi ad invicem, dicentes:
Therefore, the Jews debated among themselves,
Quomodo potest hic nobis carnem suam dare ad manducandum?
saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
And so, Jesus said to them:
nisi manducaveritis carnem Filii hominis, et biberitis ejus sanguinem,
unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood,
you will not have life in you.
Qui manducat meam carnem, et bibit meum sanguinem, habet vitam æternam:
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life,
et ego resuscitabo eum in novissimo die.
and I will raise him up on the last day.
Caro enim mea vere est cibus:
For my flesh is true food,
et sanguis meus, vere est potus;
and my blood is true drink.
qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem,
and drinks my blood abides in me,
Just as the living Father has sent me
and I live because of the Father,
the same shall live because of me.
Hic est panis qui de cælo descendit.
This is the bread that descends from heaven.
Non sicut manducaverunt patres vestri manna,
It is not like the manna that your fathers ate,
Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum.
Whoever eats this bread shall live forever.”
Hæc dixit in synagoga docens, in Capharnaum.
He said these things when he was teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.
Multi ergo audientes ex discipulis ejus,
Therefore, many of his disciples, upon hearing this,
and, “Who is able to listen to it?”
Sciens autem Jesus apud semetipsum quia murmurarent de hoc discipuli ejus,
But Jesus, knowing within himself that his disciples were murmuring about this,
si ergo videritis Filium hominis ascendentem ubi erat prius?
Then what if you were to see the Son of man ascending to where he was before?
It is the Spirit who gives life.
The flesh does not offer anything of benefit.
verba quæ ego locutus sum vobis,
The words that I have spoken to you are spirit
Sed sunt quidam ex vobis qui non credunt.
But there are some among you who do not believe.”
Sciebat enim ab initio Jesus qui essent non credentes,
For Jesus knew from the beginning who were unbelieving
and which one would betray him.
quia nemo potest venire ad me,
I said to you that no one is able to come to me,
nisi fuerit ei datum a Patre meo.
unless it has been given to him by my Father.”
Ex hoc multi discipulorum ejus abierunt retro:
After this, many of his disciples went back,
et jam non cum illo ambulabant.
and they no longer walked with him.
“Do you also want to go away?”
You have the words of eternal life.
et cognovimus quia tu es Christus Filius Dei.
and we recognize that you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
et ex vobis unus diabolus est?
And yet one among you is a devil.”
Now he was speaking about Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
For this one, even though he was one of the twelve,
